title: Vatha Kuzhambu
intro: Let me know if you want to see different types of Kuzhambu on the feed?

items: 1 lemon ball size tamarind soaked in 3 cups water
1 tbsp rice flour mixed with 1/4 cup water

method: Prep work: add the tamarind to a bowl and top with 3 cups hot water and set aside for 30 minutes
Squeeze the tamarind with the water once its warm to touch and then drain the water squeezing out the tamarind goodness and set aside
In a pan add oil to the pan then the mustard seeds, chana dal and urad dal and let it cook - the seeds will splutter and the dals will be mildly brown - dont let it burn
Add in the garllic cloves and the shallots ( if you feel the shallots are big, then you can cut them in half too , they simmer in the gravy so well )
Once a few minutes of saute is done, add in the kozhambu podi and tamarind water and combine
This will now simmer for 20-30 minutes
Once thats done add in the sugar / jaggery + rice flour mix and let it thicken
This will take 2-4 minutes, then add salt to taste and its ready
This is a very tangy gravy so its eaten with rice but don’t serve it to yourself like you would a dal as it can be overpowering
Tastes great with a large serving of rice and a ladel or two of this kozhambu
tips: This is not the most traditional style vatha kozhamabu that usually uses Sundakkai in the recipe but i didnt have it and ive seen more detailed recipes with alot more steps but this is the recipe my mother in law showed me and i follow it!

Nutrition: 
C: 24 | F: 4 | P: 4
Calories: 148 per serve
Serves 4

Ingredients
1 tbsp sesame oil 
1/2 tbsp mustard seeds
1 tbsp channa dal
1 tbsp urad dal
10-12 cloves of garlic
100 grams shallots or 2 sliced onions 
1 lemon ball size tamarind soaked in 3 cups water
2 tbsp kuzhambu podi 
1 tbsp jaggery / brown sugar 
salt, to taste
1 tbsp rice flour mixed with 1/4 cup water

Method 
prep work: add the tamarind to a bowl and top with 3 cups hot water and set aside for 30 minutes
squeeze the tamarind with the water once its warm to touch and then drain the water squeezing out the tamarind goodness and set aside 
in a pan add oil to the pan then the mustard seeds, chana dal and urad dal and let it cook - the seeds will splutter and the dals will be mildly brown - dont let it burn 
add in the garllic cloves and the shallots ( if you feel the shallots are big, then you can cut them in half too , they simmer in the gravy so well ) 
once a few minutes of saute is done, add in the kozhambu podi and tamarind water and combine 
this will now simmer for 20-30 minutes
once thats done add in the sugar / jaggery + rice flour mix and let it thicken 
this will take 2-4 minutes, then add salt to taste and its ready 
Serving: 
this is a very tangy gravy so its eaten with rice but don’t serve it to yourself like you would a dal as it can be overpowering
tastes great with a large serving of rice and a ladel or two of this kozhambu 
Note: 
this is not the most traditional style vatha kozhamabu that usually uses Sundakkai in the recipe but i didnt have it and ive seen more detailed recipes with alot more steps but this is the recipe my mother in law showed me and i follow it!
